lines.text: Every December, I work nights at a Christmas tree lot, out on the edge of town.
The owner, old Hank, gave me one rule on my very first shift.
See that tall one in the back corner? The one with no price tag?
It's not for sale. If anyone asks for it after midnight... say no. Don't let them touch it.
For two weeks, nobody came. Just me, a space heater, and four hundred trees.
Then, a little after one in the morning... the front gate creaked open.
A family walked in. A mother, a father, two small kids. All in matching red scarves.
They didn't look at a single tree. They walked straight to the back corner.
We'll take this one, the father said. It wants to come home with us.
I told them no. They just smiled... and kept smiling.
Snow was coming down hard that night... but not one flake landed on them.
I locked myself in the trailer until the sun came up.
In the morning, the family was gone. No tire tracks. No footprints.
But the tall tree... was standing two rows closer to my trailer.
